findings.evidence: Basic.lean:77 `theorem integrable_inv_add ... (ht : 0 < t) : Integrable (fun x : ℝ≥0 => (t + (x : ℝ))⁻¹) μ` is public; CompleteBernstein.lean:98 proves the div version by `simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv] using (integrable_inv_add hμ ht).const_mul t`. Bernstein.lean works throughout with `∫ x, t / (t + x) ∂μ` and has no such lemma available.
findings.fix: Move it public to `Stieltjes/Basic.lean` immediately after `integrable_inv_add`, e.g. `theorem integrable_div_add {μ : Measure ℝ≥0} (hμ : Integrable stieltjesWeight μ) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : Integrable (fun x : ℝ≥0 => t / (t + x)) μ`.
findings.issue: `private lemma integrable_div_add : Integrable stieltjesWeight μ → 0 ≤ t → Integrable (fun x : ℝ≥0 => t / (t + x)) μ` is general Stieltjes-kernel infrastructure: nothing in its statement or proof mentions complete Bernstein functions (it only uses `integrable_inv_add`). Hiding it here denies it to every other consumer of `stieltjesBernsteinTransform`.

findings.evidence: grep for `exists_isBernsteinFunction_eqOn_mul` across `code/` returns only its definition (Bernstein.lean:323) and its docstring bullet (Bernstein.lean:54) — no in-repo uses. Its proof body is identical to lines 226-229 of the new file modulo the weaker predicate.
findings.fix: Delete `IsStieltjesFunction.exists_isBernsteinFunction_eqOn_mul` and its Main-declarations bullet (Bernstein.lean:54); consumers use the new iff plus `.isBernsteinFunction`.
findings.issue: `IsStieltjesFunction.exists_isBernsteinFunction_eqOn_mul` is now a strictly weaker duplicate of the forward direction of the new `isStieltjesFunction_iff_exists_isCompleteBernsteinFunction_eqOn_mul` (same existential, weaker predicate, obtainable via `IsCompleteBernsteinFunction.isBernsteinFunction`). Two entry points for the same fact, the weaker one more discoverable.

findings.evidence: Bernstein.lean:86-89 has `@[simp] theorem stieltjesBernsteinTransform_zero ... = a`, but no representation-level counterpart exists in the new file (no `_zero`/`apply_zero` accessor in CompleteBernstein.lean:73-91).
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] lemma apply_zero (h : RepresentsCompleteBernstein μ a b f) : f 0 = a := by simp [h.eq_stieltjesBernsteinTransform le_rfl]` in the `RepresentsCompleteBernstein` namespace.
findings.issue: Missing the characteristic boundary lemma `f 0 = a`, the one fact that distinguishes the `[0, ∞)` extension from the Stieltjes function and that the module docstring advertises twice (lines 25-26, 216). Consumers must route through `eq_stieltjesBernsteinTransform` and the transform's own simp lemma.

findings.evidence: Bernstein/Basic.lean:199 `theorem isBernsteinFunction_id : IsBernsteinFunction (fun t : ℝ => t)`; the other two new examples (CompleteBernstein.lean:239, 257) also use lambdas.
findings.fix: State it as `IsCompleteBernsteinFunction (fun t : ℝ => t)` (name `isCompleteBernsteinFunction_id` unchanged), matching `isBernsteinFunction_id`.
findings.issue: `isCompleteBernsteinFunction_id : IsCompleteBernsteinFunction id` is phrased with `id`, while the sibling example one file up is phrased with a lambda, so the two do not unify syntactically and `rw`/`simp` with lemmas stated for `fun t : ℝ => t` will not apply to it.

summary: The new predicates carry a reasonable accessor/closure surface, but a general Stieltjes-kernel integrability lemma is hidden as `private` in this downstream file instead of living public next to its sibling, and the PR leaves a now-strictly-subsumed duplicate of the correspondence in `Stieltjes/Bernstein.lean`.
